ai.description: This caecilian reaches 20–25 cm. It is dark purplish-brown with a paler venter. Distinctive features include a protruding snout, visible primary annuli, and a terminal shield on the tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Uraeotyphlus malabaricus* is uniquely distinguished by its distinct, dark-pigmented head that contrasts sharply with its paler, purplish-grey body.
ai.habitat: The Malabar Caecilian inhabits moist, shaded soil and leaf litter within tropical evergreen forests and plantations across the Western Ghats, typically above 600 meters.
ai.behavior: The Malabar Caecilian is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, emerging from moist soil to hunt for earthworms and small invertebrates during the rainy season.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Malabar caecilian is oviparous, laying small clutches of eggs in underground nests. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, with females guarding the eggs.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Malabar Caecilian is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu at elevations between 200 and 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Malabar Caecilian produces a high-pitched, rhythmic series of clicks or chirps, typically emitted from within moist soil or leaf litter in Western Ghats forests.
